en: Even the water is holding its breath.
af: Selfs die water hou sy asem op.
flag_reason: `metsi a khomaretse moea` says the water is clinging to air, not holding its breath.

en: The horizon looks like a movie finale.
af: Die horison lyk soos 'n fliek se slottoneel.
flag_reason: `leholimo` is the sky, not the horizon; the specific visual boundary is lost.

en: Somebody's birthday-candle wish just paid out.
af: Iemand het reggewens by die verjaarsdagkoek.
flag_reason: `Takatso ea motho ea kerese` misattaches the birthday candle to the person and does not form a valid birthday-candle wish.

en: Rain turns every South African driver back into a learner. Hazards on, dignity off.
af: Reën verander elke Suid-Afrikaanse bestuurder terug in 'n leerling.
flag_reason: `Hazards di tsoha` says the hazard lights rise/get up, not switch on.

en: One drought in living memory and now every downpour is a lottery win.
af: Drie jaar se droogte-geheue en skielik is elke bui 'n lotto-wen.
flag_reason: `eo re sa e hopolang` says the drought is one we do not remember, reversing `in living memory`.

en: To the dam levels! Every downpour is a round on the house.
af: Op die damvlakke! Elke bui is 'n rondte op die huis.
flag_reason: `round ea ntlo` literally makes the shower a round belonging to the house, not a free round `on the house`.

en: Sleep tight, dams. You worked hard today.
af: Slaap lekker, damme. Julle het vandag hard gewerk.
flag_reason: `Robala` is a singular imperative addressed to plural `matamo`; the addressee agreement is wrong.

en: Grey is also a colour, says my ma. Today I believe her.
af: Grys is ook 'n kleur, sê my ma. Vandag glo ek haar.
flag_reason: `ho bolela mme` is not the idiomatic/reporting construction `says my mother` and also leaves `mme` orthographically ambiguous.

en: Streetlights on early tonight, and not a single complaint.
af: Die straatligte gaan vroeg aan en niemand kla nie.
flag_reason: `tletlebo` is singular but is quantified with class-5 `le le leng`; the agreement is malformed.

en: The evening is tiptoeing in on socks.
af: Die aand kom binne op sokkies.
flag_reason: `a hatella butle` means presses/steps slowly and does not specifically convey tiptoeing.

en: Cape Town sends solidarity. And a spare cap.
af: Kaapstad stuur sterkte. En 'n ekstra pet.
flag_reason: `Le cap e teng` only says there is also a cap; it drops the fact that the cap is a spare.

en: The mountain has set the table. For two hundred guests.
af: Die berg het die tafel gedek. Vir tweehonderd gaste.
flag_reason: `Thaba e aliloe tafole` makes the mountain the passive recipient of laying and does not say that it set the table.

en: The Cape Doctor is working straight through lunch.
af: Die Kaapse Dokter werk deur etenstyd.
flag_reason: `ho theosa le lunch` is a literal down/along-lunch construction, not working straight through lunch.

en: The boats are staying in. Take the hint.
af: Die bote bly binne. Vat die wenk.
flag_reason: `mokgwa` means manner/way; `Nka mokgwa` does not mean `take the hint`.

en: Turns out the Doctor also works night shift.
af: Blyk die Dokter werk óók nagskof.
flag_reason: `Ho hlaha ngaka` says a doctor appears and also drops the named Cape Doctor; it does not mean `turns out`.

en: The tablecloth is pressed and ready for tomorrow's service.
af: Die tafeldoek is gestryk en reg vir môre se diens.
flag_reason: `ten'ehile` is a form of `teneha` (be annoyed), not pressed/ironed; the tablecloth is given the wrong state.

en: The clouds are rushing like they're late for something.
af: Die wolke jaag asof hulle laat is vir iets.
flag_reason: `a siiloe ke ho hong` says the clouds were left behind by something, not that they are late for something.

en: First one up puts the kettle on. That's the law.
af: Eerste een op moet die ketel aansit. Dis die wet.
flag_reason: `o tuka ketlele` says the first person up burns the kettle, not puts/switches it on.

en: Cape cold is wet cold. It moves into your bones and unpacks.
af: Kaapse koue is nat koue. Dit klim in jou bene en pak uit.
flag_reason: `ho phutholohe` means relax/unfold, not unpack belongings after moving into one's bones.

en: Prettiest blue sky in the country, and it feels like a fridge with a view.
af: Mooiste blou lug in die land, en dit voel soos 'n yskas met uitsig.
flag_reason: `letala/botala` means green, not blue; the central sky colour is wrong.

en: Winter sun: all of the light, none of the heat. Nice try, sun.
af: Winterson: al die lig, nul van die hitte. Mooi probeer, son.
flag_reason: `Mohlolo o motle` means a good/beautiful marvel, not `nice try`.

en: The seagulls sound furious about it. Same, seagulls. Same.
af: Die meeue klink kwaad. Dieselfde, meeue. Dieselfde.
flag_reason: `dikoekoe` denotes quails/speckled birds, not seagulls; the existing corpus occurrence repeats the same animal-word defect.

en: Last one home lights the fire. Drive, friend, drive.
af: Laaste een by die huis maak die kaggel aan. Ry, vriend, ry.
flag_reason: `o tuka mollo` says the last person burns/is burning the fire rather than lights it.

en: The blesbok wear no scarves and file no complaints. We could learn something. We won't, but we could.
af: Die blesbokke dra nie serpe nie en kla ook nie. Ons kan iets leer. Ons gaan nie, maar ons kan.
flag_reason: `Diblesbok` fuses the Sesotho plural prefix directly to the loan without the boundary used for code-switched nouns.

en: Wet and cold is the Cape's winter recipe. Two ingredients, every time.
af: Nat en koud is die Kaap se winterresep. Twee bestanddele, elke keer.
flag_reason: `Metsi le serame` means water and cold, not wet and cold.

en: Today's sky: freshly washed, ice-pressed.
af: Vandag se lug is skoongewas en yskoud gestryk.
flag_reason: `tenwa` means be annoyed/irritated, not pressed; `ice-pressed` is mistranslated.

en: Those sheets are coming off the line in cardboard form.
af: Lakens gaan vandag in kartonvorm afgehaal word.
flag_reason: `sekgutlwana` is a small corner/booth, not cardboard form; the sheets image does not survive.

en: Orange flowers, blue sky, blue lips.
af: Oranje blomme, blou lug, blou lippe.
flag_reason: `letala/botala` means green, not blue; the central sky colour is wrong.

en: The bluer the sky, the colder the truth.
af: Hoe blouer die lug, hoe kouer die waarheid.
flag_reason: `letala/botala` means green, not blue; the central sky colour is wrong.

en: The Karoo is opening its roof for the night. Dress warm for the show.
af: Die Karoo maak nou die dak oop. Trek warm aan vir die vertoning.
flag_reason: `Apara ka mocheso` says dress with heat, not dress warmly for the show.

en: The frost has already started its shift. By dawn the lawn will be glass.
af: Die ryp is klaar besig. Teen dagbreek is die grasperk 'n spieël.
flag_reason: `qadile` is an unattested misspelling in this context; the standard past form of `qala` is `qalile`.

en: Tomorrow's first task: five minutes of windscreen scraping in your work clothes.
af: Môreoggend se eerste taak: vyf minute ys krap in jou kerkklere.
flag_reason: `ho hoahoa` is a building/construction form, not scraping ice from a windscreen.

en: The oldest tree has the best seats. As always.
af: Die oudste boom het die beste sitplekke. Soos altyd.
flag_reason: `se seholo ka ho fetisisa` means the biggest tree, not the oldest tree.

en: The first sip after a 35-degree day should honestly be taxable.
af: Die eerste sluk ná 'n 35-grade dag behoort eerlikwaar belasbaar te wees.
flag_reason: `Selumo` could not be attested as a Sesotho word for a sip and appears to be a guessed content noun.

en: Ice cream at eight isn't dessert, it's a recovery plan.
af: Roomys om agtuur is nie nagereg nie, dis 'n herstelplan.
flag_reason: The English says ice cream at eight, but `ka robong` changes the time to nine.

en: The sun only sets after eight. Summer knows how to stretch an evening.
af: Die son sak eers ná agt. Somer weet hoe om 'n aand te rek.
flag_reason: The English says the sun sets after eight, but `kamora robong` changes the time to after nine.

en: The farm is still there. We're all just taking each other's word for it.
af: Die plaas is nog daar. Ons vat maar mekaar se woord daarvoor.
flag_reason: `re nka feela lentsoe la e mong` is a word-for-word `take another's word` construction rather than an idiomatic reliance expression.

en: Visibility: poor. Vibes: untouchable.
af: Sig: swak. Vibes: onaantasbaar.
flag_reason: `ha di ame` means the vibes do not touch/affect; it does not convey that the vibes themselves are untouchable.

en: The nearest neighbours are thirty kilometres away and tonight they can see you even less.
af: Die naaste bure is dertig kilometer weg en vanaand kan hulle jou nog minder sien.
flag_reason: `ba o bona le ho feta hanyane` combines `more` with `a little` and obscures the intended `see you even less`.

en: Morning people might be onto something. Don't tell them.
af: Oggendmense is dalk oor iets reg. Sê dit net vir niemand nie.
flag_reason: `ba nepile ho hong` means they are right about something, not that they may be onto/discovering something.

en: Zero drama in the sky. Highly unusual. Gladly accepted.
af: Die dag begin sonder drama. Verdag, maar ons vat dit.
flag_reason: `Ha ho tloaeleha` is a malformed impersonal construction for `highly unusual`.

en: Karoo sky: same flawless blue for the next 400 km. Guaranteed.
af: Karoo-blou: presies dieselfde perfekte kleur van hier tot môre.
flag_reason: `letala/botala` means green, not blue; the central sky colour is wrong.

en: Be honest — you opened this app to confirm Saturday's braai.
af: Check jy die weer, of check jy of Saterdag se braai aan is? Presies.
flag_reason: `Ba tšepahala` means `they are honest`; it is not the singular imperative `be honest`.

en: Nobody's called it a night. The night agrees.
af: Niemand het 'huis toe' gesê nie. Niemand gaan ook nie.
flag_reason: `Ha ho ea reng ke bosiu` says nobody says it is night; it misses the idiom `called it a night` meaning stopped for the evening.
